actual: 285 dates after the crawl, up to 2027-12-31
problem: A notice cannot be posted after it was observed. Left uncorrected these produce negative recency, i.e. universities scoring as fresher than physically possible.
fix: CENSOR to recency=0 and flag with notice_date_future - do not delete the rows; the presence of a dated notice is still real information.

problem: Unusable AND prestige-leaking: the project's core claim requires ranking on website quality independently of institutional reputation.
fix: Drop from the modelling dataset.

problem: Unusable: 8 values cannot support any analysis. Also an external prestige benchmark, excluded from the primary model by design.
fix: Drop from the modelling dataset.

expected: Count of broken links, with a denominator to form a rate
actual: 81.1% zeros, no total-links column, one extreme value of 1129 against a second-highest of 59
problem: Zero is ambiguous between 'checked, none found' and 'checker did not run'. Without a denominator, 2 broken links on a 20-link page cannot be distinguished from 2 on a 500-link page.
fix: Read 0 as verified-absence (ok=True and render_error=null for EVERY row - no evidence of checker failure anywhere in the crawl metadata). Use log1p + winsorisation at p99 plus a broken_links_present binary. Absence of a denominator is a permanent documented limitation.

expected: Collectors overlap across regions so their effects can be separated
actual: Perfect 1:1 mapping - zero overlap between collectors and regions
problem: 'African websites are slower' and 'M6 had a slower connection' are statistically indistinguishable in this design. No post-hoc method can separate them.
fix: Report as an UNRESOLVABLE limitation. Mitigate with region-standardised load time and leave-one-region-out validation; never claim a causal regional difference in any timing-derived measure.

expected: Prestige variables excluded from the quality model
actual: Both are binary PRESENCE flags, not rank values
problem: Easy to over-correct: these measure whether the site displays a credibility signal, which is a genuine (if weak and trivially gamed) website attribute. Dropping them discards real website information; weighting them normally smuggles in prestige.
fix: KEEP as website features but assign the lowest rubric tier (near-zero weight).

expected: Same website -> same measured load time
actual: Re-crawls disagree by up to 3.3x (UNAM 13.46s vs 4.07s) while agreeing on 99% of all other attributes
problem: Load time measures the collector's network conditions, not the website. It is also perfectly confounded with region (one collector per region).
fix: Region-standardise (z-score within region); report all rankings with AND without it.

problem: Presented as continuous but actually a coarse rule-based heuristic. Scaling it as continuous implies precision the measurement does not have.
fix: Recode as a 6-level ORDINAL feature.

problem: Missingness is INFORMATIVE - no dated notice found is itself a freshness signal, not an absent measurement. Imputing a date would erase that signal.
fix: Keep null; derive notice_recency_days plus an explicit a18_missing indicator.

expected: Notice-board flag, timestamp flag and date agree
actual: 382 rows have a date with the board flag off; 156 have the board flag on with no date
problem: The three notice fields disagree on whether a notice board exists. Using them as three independent binaries triple-counts a contradictory signal.
fix: Collapse into ONE ordinal notice_evidence (0 none / 1 undated board / 2 dated board / 3 dated and recent) that reconciles the contradiction explicitly.

actual: Mass piles up exactly on the schema maximum (20 / 10 / 20)
problem: Right-censored at the extractor cap. Treating the cap as a true count makes 'more' look monotonically better when the cap actually signals an undifferentiated dump.
fix: Apply non-linear (inverted-U / diminishing-return) rubric curves rather than linear scaling; document the cap in the feature dictionary.

actual: 10 labels are multi-country buckets covering 170 rows
problem: A 'country ranking' over a bucket such as Sub-Saharan Africa (42 universities across many countries) is not a country ranking at all.
fix: Add country_is_bucket; publish country-level rankings ONLY for the 19 real countries with >=20 universities.

expected: Events flag agrees with the event count
actual: 327 rows flag events with count 0; 158 count events with the flag off
problem: Same double-counting problem as the notice fields.
fix: Collapse into one ordinal event_evidence.
